rootCause.explanation: Header renders two independent ThemeToggle instances (desktop and mobile), each with its own useState. The THEME_CHANGE_EVENT is dispatched but never subscribed to. A hidden instance keeps a stale 'system' state, and its matchMedia listener re-applies 'system' on an OS scheme change, overriding the user's explicit light/dark choice made in the other instance. This violates the explicit light/dark acceptance criteria.
evidence: ThemeToggle.jsx:19 useState('system') per instance; no listener for THEME_CHANGE_EVENT
ThemeToggle.jsx:25-35 effect depends on closed-over `theme` state and applies 'system' unconditionally
ThemeToggle.jsx:42 event dispatched with no subscriber
Code review finding MAJOR on ThemeToggle.jsx:18; QA and security passed (48/48 tests, build OK)

report.loopEvidence: First attempt; no previous triage or attempts to compare.
developerHints: In ThemeToggle.jsx add a useEffect that subscribes to THEME_CHANGE_EVENT on window and calls setTheme(event.detail), and also listens to the window 'storage' event (setTheme(getStoredTheme(window.localStorage)) when event.key === THEME_STORAGE_KEY); remove both on cleanup. This keeps the mobile and desktop instances in sync.

Make the matchMedia handleChange (ThemeToggle.jsx:30-32) defensive: re-read `getStoredTheme(window.localStorage)` and only call applyTheme('system', ...) when the stored value is 'system', so a stale instance can never override an explicit light/dark choice. Do not rely on the closed-over `theme` state.

Avoid the 'System default' flash: initialise state lazily with `useState(() => typeof window === 'undefined' ? 'system' : getStoredTheme(window.localStorage))` is unsafe for SSR hydration under client:load, so instead keep the useEffect init but it is acceptable; at minimum do not regress the existing behaviour.

Extract the cycle-and-persist step (nextTheme + storeTheme + applyTheme) into a helper in ui/src/lib/theme.js, e.g. cycleStoredTheme(current, {storage, root, matchMedia}) returning the new theme, and add unit tests in ui/src/lib/__tests__/theme.test.js (explicit imports, helpers at end of file). Also unit-test any new stored-theme re-resolve helper. Do not weaken or remove existing tests.

Use `var` for local variable declarations inside functions in the new/modified JS files as AGENTS.md requires (QA minor finding), e.g. in theme.js, ThemeToggle.jsx and theme.test.js; keep module-level constants as const.
Optional: remove the redundant `.dark .border-t.border-gray-100` rule in ui/src/styles/global.css, since `.dark .border-gray-100` already covers it.
report.summary: QA and security pass, but the code review found a real correctness defect: two unsynchronised ThemeToggle instances can re-apply a stale 'system' theme over an explicit user choice. This is a fixable production-code defect on attempt 1 of 3, so route back to the developer with concrete sync and re-read-from-storage hints, plus the minor var-convention cleanup.
